title: MIT AI forecasts extreme weather without historical data
slides: Can AI forecast storms with zero past weather data?
MIT's model learns from physics, not history.
It predicts extremes even in entirely new climates.
This means better forecasts where data is scarce.
Test it on your next severe weather event.
thread_text:
1. Zero data, real forecasts

MIT's new AI predicts storms using only physics, skipping historical weather records entirely.

2. Physics as the teacher

Instead of learning from past events, the model understands atmospheric laws, so it works in climates it has never seen.

3. Extremes in new worlds

It can forecast severe weather in places with no weather stations or past data, like remote regions or future climates.

4. Data-scarce regions win

This could save lives in developing countries where reliable forecasts are rare, giving early warnings for floods or heatwaves.

5. Test it yourself

Take a weather event on your radar and check if current models fail where data is thin. Would this approach change your action?

instagram.caption:
A storm warning system that works even where no weather station has ever existed — MIT just built one that learns from physics alone, not historical records. 🌪️

Instead of studying past weather data, this model understands the laws of the atmosphere itself. So it can predict extremes in climates it has never encountered — remote regions, developing countries, even future conditions under climate change.

For anyone covering weather or climate: this means forecasts in data-scarce zones won't depend on decades of records anymore. Your reporting could rely on tools that work from scratch.

What would you do with reliable warnings in a place that's never had them? 📡
